entities.summary:
Furia Sabinia Tranquillina was the Empress of Rome and wife of Emperor Gordian III. She was the young daughter of the Praetorian Prefect Timesitheus by an unknown wife.

Tranquillina's rise to power began when her father, Timesitheus, became the Praetorian Prefect in 238 CE. He was tasked with supporting Emperor Maximinus Thrax against his rivals, and Tranquillina played a key role in securing Gordian III's succession. She was just 15 years old at the time.

In 244 CE, Tranquillina became Empress when her husband Gordian III died in battle against the Sassanid Empire. Her rule was short-lived, as she died shortly after giving birth to their son, Gordian IV.

Tranquillina's legacy is complex and multifaceted. She played a crucial role in securing her family's power and influence during a tumultuous period of Roman history. Her impact can still be seen in the Roman Empire's later years, particularly in the reigns of her successors.

The legacy of Furia Sabinia Tranquillina continues to fascinate historians and scholars today. She remains one of the most enigmatic figures of the late Roman Empire, a testament to the intrigue and politics that defined this period of human history.

Tranquillina's impact on history can be seen in several ways: her role in securing Gordian III's succession, her position as Empress during a time of great turmoil, and her legacy in the later years of the Roman Empire.
